import framebuf
w, h = 240, 320
# GS4_HMSB packs 2px/byte, each row padded UP to a whole byte -- ((w+1)//2)
# is the real per-row byte count display_spi's own codegen expects
# (Math.ceil(width/2) there), not a flat w*h/2. w=240 is even here so the
# two formulas happen to agree, but this is written the general way on
# purpose -- see display-spi.ts's header for why a flat formula silently
# breaks on an odd width (TiDAL's 135).
stride = (w + 1) // 2
buf = bytearray(stride * h)
fb = framebuf.FrameBuffer(buf, w, h, framebuf.GS4_HMSB)
# Default palette indices (display_spi's own DEFAULT_PALETTE_GS4, unset
# here on purpose to also exercise the no-palette-property default path):
# 0 black 1 white 2 red 3 green 4 blue 5 yellow 6 cyan 7 magenta
fb.fill(0)
fb.text('GS4 240x320', 8, 8, 1)
fb.fill_rect(0, 40, w, 60, 2)
fb.fill_rect(0, 100, w, 60, 3)
fb.fill_rect(0, 160, w, 60, 4)
fb.fill_rect(0, 220, w, 60, 6)
fb.ellipse(120, 280, 35, 35, 5, True)
# Send the bytearray itself: bytes(buf) would need a second full-size copy,
# which a fragmented ESP32 heap may not have in one piece.
msg['payload'] = buf
return msg
